Archives and images. Almost everything on screen lives in .xb archives full of .gim textures (4/8-bit palettised images). We wrote tools to unpack an archive, replace single entries, and repack it byte-compatibly.

The US game as a reference. Hot Shots Golf: Open Tee is the same game under the hood, so we used it as our wording guide ("Loyalty", "Everybody's Golf"...) and, where a US image sat in the same place with the same size, we copied its artwork across. Where the US art did not fit (different layout, or the Japanese edition has things the US one lacks, like the Coca-Cola elements), we drew new English text in matching styles.

Clipping. The game draws each Japanese text image through a rectangle exactly as wide as the Japanese text, so a longer English word is cut off mid-letter. That produced bugs like "Stroke Pla" and "Autumn Pag"; fixing them meant measuring every label against its Japanese slot and squeezing or shortening only what needed it.

Code patches. A few things cannot be done with images alone. The Japanese stroke counter drew "number + 打 + 目" ("3rd stroke"), so we patched the game's code with small trampolines into unused space to draw "3rd Stroke" and lay out the "Remaining" distance like the US game. Along the way we hit (and fixed) a crash caused by patched code overlapping data, and learned that the right-hand opponent's text starts at a different position depending on game state.

This project was made with the help of an AI assistant (Claude, by Anthropic), which did some of the reverse-engineering, tool-writing, image editing and patch building under Mr-Shizzy's direction and testing. Wording and every change were reviewed and play-tested by a human. Bug reports are welcome.

Translation units and globals. DemoSequenceItem ( 2173c4 , 2174d0 ) is a separate unit after the sequence unit. If it is in the same file, release gets inlined into clear .

Inline helpers change optimization order. clear matches only when the final free goes through an inline demo_safe_free(owner, ptr) helper. Writing the null check directly in clear changes the loop: the original peels the first release and reloads items at the top of each later iteration.
Each point is copied word by word through per-iteration references ( DemoPoint& dst = points[i] ). A struct assignment turns into 64-bit copies.

217188 . The allocation descriptor comes from an inline demo_alloc helper. Inlined stack slots go first, so the 40-byte resource frame lands below the descriptor, as in the original. The size is computed into a local first ( unsigned int size = sizeof(DemoSequenceItem) * count; ), which gives the original instruction order.

Demo overrides unit ( event/demo_overrides.cpp , 2581d4 – 258970 ). It ends with the static initializer 258970 , which constructs the two queue workers at c8aef8 and registers their array destructor 258944 with __cxa_atexit . So the workers are defined here, which is why the queue unit refers to them as an external hidden global. 45de40 / 45de54 are the Worker constructor and destructor. apply_demo_tuning lists its cases in the order 2, 0x20, 0x13.

Demo track items ( event/demo_track_items.cpp , 25b828 – 25bd64 ). These bodies are decided by how stores merge, which depends on field types. TrackKey 's field at +0x10 is a float : a float zero doesn't merge with the integer -1 index stores beside it.
apply_track_light : the range-reduction selects use inverted compares ( !(a >= kPi) ), which gives fcsel lt . dy is computed before dx . The no-angle path reads the image size inline.

Light table set ( event/demo_light_table_set.cpp , 25ffe8 – 2605d0 ). It holds the light system's TrackResources at +8 ; the three handles are the channels' tables, so TrackLightTable derives from RefObject . The empty 25cd50 is ~TrackResources . 25c240 ( TrackSlot ) default-constructs each TrackLightSet 's storage before placement. The LightAllocator is a DemoOwner . ResourceFrame::open returns unsigned char , which gives the caller's and #0xff . The frame unit still matches.

Light entries ( event/demo_light_entry.cpp , 260648 – 260740 ). These are textured sprites, 0xd0 bytes each, holding a reference-counted texture. They are a separate unit because the table-set loops call their constructor and destructor. bind copies a 64-byte table of four RGBA colors ( 7f50f0 , mapped as .rodata ) and stores the allocator in a global (GOT c2a640 ).

Demo effect pool ( event/demo_effect_pool.cpp , 26086c – 26303c ). A 0x12f0-byte singleton (GOT c2a648 ) holding four arrays of 28 effect slots (two 0x28-byte kinds, two 0x20-byte kinds), 28 caption nodes, a counter node and a LightResource . The effect-manager types moved to include/event/demo_effects.h . LightEffect takes its mode (0x10 in the light system, 0x11 here).

The constructor assigns everything in its body, after the LightResource member is constructed. Slots are reset by inline reset() helpers. The destructor calls finalize() , so destroy_demo_effect_pool finalizes twice, as in the original.

draw_marker has to be defined in this unit: the original calls it without setting x0 (dead-argument elimination). render_marker is called with x0 set even though it never reads it, and it is also called from 298c3c . So it is an inline member (linkonce, which the optimizer leaves alone), emitted where update_markers first references it. DemoEffectPool::draw ( 26302c ) calls both the same way, so it belongs to this unit too.

Whole source-data placements must match the retail fragment kind and extent, belong to reconstructed text in that image, and cannot place a source section twice. The linker asserts the emitted extent and rejects orphan runtime sections or common storage needing placement support. Partial/sparse source sections and source global constructor/destructor lists still require further integration support.

PsyQ 4.1 LIBCD/SYS (23 functions), LIBCD/TOC (two functions), and LIBCARD/INIT (three functions) are also fully imported. Their complete text, read-only data, and initialized data are native-linked with explicit function and data bindings, byte-verified, then checked again in all five final images. This includes the CD parameter table at 0x800B5E6C and the card member's data at 0x800B5E5C, whose boundaries do not coincide with the old scaffold labels.

Additional complete members now linked are LIBAPI/COUNTER (five root-counter functions and 32 data bytes at 0x800B6374), LIBCD/EVENT ( CdInit and 32 read-only bytes at 0x8010E248), and LIBSN/_UDIVMOD ( __udivmoddi4 and its 256-byte read-only table at 0x8010DBF8). Each section's entire original byte sequence has one matching retail placement; native relocations, function addresses, scaffold extents, and all five complete images are checked as usual.

The BSS path also imports LIBAPI/SENDPAD (two functions), LIBAPI/CHCLRPAD , LIBCARD/END , and LIBGTE/PATCHGTE . Their respective 16-byte storage ranges at 0x8012FFB0, 0x8012FFC0, 0x80130130, and 0x80132590 are explicitly owned and placed. Complete original text, internal patch data, external relocations, and the final images match; none of these routines is reconstructed in C.

LIBCARD/A76 ( StopCARD2 ) and the complete 464-byte LIBCARD/PATCH member are imported together. PATCH's 152-byte leading code region was attached to the old StopCARD2 scaffold; explicit prefix ownership preserves it and its internal data/jump labels. Label aliases are emitted only after validating the complete scaffold extent, including the neighbor's verified prefix. PATCH's 16-byte BSS is pinned at 0x80130120, and all five linked images still match retail.

LIBETC/PAD adds PadInit , PadRead , and PadStop . Its private 16-byte BSS is at 0x8012FF80, while the four-byte common PadIdentifier is at 0x80135220. Original PSYLINK accepts an explicit binding for the common without modifying the archive object. The importer checks its original XBSS size, retail/native address, and a separate final-image allocation; common and private allocations share the same bounds/overlap checks. All five images match with both present.

The complete LIBETC/INTR , LIBETC/INTR_DMA , and LIBAPI/C114 members add 15 entries (12 original exports and three internal entries). INTR's 4,352-byte initialized section at 0x800B42EC includes relocated callback pointers; the entire linked data matches retail. Its final internal scaffold owns C114's eight-byte prefix, and this ownership must pass the same contiguous full-member and complete-scaffold checks as named owners. All five images remain exact.

LIBCD/BIOS contributes 13 entries (12 archive exports plus its leading internal routine). Its 5,984 text bytes at 0x8001B43C, 592 read-only bytes at 0x8010E278, and 800 initialized bytes at 0x800B5EEC all match after native relocation. Thirteen initialized exports independently agree on that data base. Its private 48-byte BSS is placed at 0x80130140, and the four-byte StMode common is placed at 0x801351D8. Both allocations and all five complete images are verified.

LIBCD/ISO9660 , LIBCD/CDREAD , and LIBC/C24 add 13 entries (seven archive exports and six internal entries). ISO9660 supplies its complete 9,216-byte private BSS at 0x80130170, plus initialized state and read-only strings. CDREAD's leading 812 bytes were attached to the strncmp scaffold; explicit prefix ownership now places them from CDREAD alongside the unchanged original strncmp member. All text, initialized sections, buffers, and five images match.

The complete LIBTAP/TAP member adds 17 entries (six archive exports and eleven internal entries), with 4,768 text bytes, 64 initialized bytes at 0x800B630C, and 128 small-BSS bytes at 0x8011C90C. Its code uses absolute references to that small-BSS section; a probe placed 16 bytes higher exposed 27 relocated-word mismatches. Correct section placement resolves all of them without modifying instructions. Every native section and all five final images match retail.

The final mixed library bridge now has complete native ownership: all 349 Sony entries come from their verified original archive members and the other 488 entries come from reconstructed GLIB/EACLIB/Climax source. No asm/nonmatchings/lib function is selected by the final main-image link.
